$comment: Derived from env-007: the same envelope and the same committed signature (kat-envelope-002-ed25519, signed by kat-keypair-001), with one change made after signing: the vendor key `extensions.com.example.debug_trace` is renamed to `extensions.com.example.audit_trace`, value unchanged. The result is schema-valid, fresh and carries only unknown `extensions` keys, so nothing before the signature check rejects it. scripts/verify-known-answer.mjs and scripts/recompute-known-answer-independent.py assert that the signature verifies over env-007's envelope and does not verify over this one. Reusing env-007's message_id is safe: each fixture runs against fresh verifier state.
description: Envelope whose `extensions` member was changed after signing. RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4: the envelope signing input is the domain-tagged JCS form of the whole envelope minus `signature`, so `extensions` is covered and a relabelled extension key breaks the signature. Under the `aitp/0.3` pipe-composed input (before issue #87) this envelope verified. Expected: INVALID_SIGNATURE.

expected.rationale: `version` is known and the member set is valid, so the RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4 check order reaches the signature. The signature was made over env-007's `extensions`; with one extension key renamed, sig_input_v2 differs and the signature does not verify.
